correctness.rationale: The cyclic binary-token folding is terminating and preserves residue modulo odd M=2^r-1; a positive reduced token sum <=M divisible by M must be M, requiring r ones. For H(t)=(2^(rt)-1)/M, odd-prime LTE establishes v_p(H(a)-H(b))=v_p(a-b) at every p|M; hence H permutes residues mod M^(k-1), providing a witness N=M(1+2H(t)) with exactly r distinct bits. Legendre gives v_2(binomial(2n,n))=s_2(n). For any odd p construct an index multiple of M^k with all base-p digits in {0,1}, so p has no central-binomial carry and cannot divide the infinite gcd. The argument covers k=1, r=2, arbitrary composite M; the binomial gcd is infinite-index, not numerical extrapolation. Independent bounded modular and odd-prime checks passed 45 r,k witnesses and 90 carry cases.

originality.rationale: O(EIS A086342) and historical work already identify minimum r for modulus M=2^r-1 at k=1; that case is not original. Elsholtz gives sparse prime multiple methods, while Clokie et al study general sturdy/flimsy multiples; the inspected theorem statements do not give equality for M^k at every k. Kummer/Legendre is prior; gcd is a corollary. A general order-lifting argument elsewhere could cover the all-k result and remains an explicit risk.
residual_risks: k=1 Mersenne minimum weight is known in OEIS and is not original; binomial gcd is a corollary of all-k sparse weight with classical valuations.
Potential unindexed general sparse-multiple power-lifting literature could predate all-k identity.
